title: Press release embargoes, explained
hook: Embargoes can make your launch, or burn a media relationship. Here's how to use them properly. ⏰

slides.title: embargoes: *how to use them* without burning bridges
what an embargo *is*
slides.body: A request that journalists don't publish before a set date and time. It gives them time to prepare a better story. It is an **agreement**, not a legal contract.

slides.title: when it's *worth it*
slides.body: Complex news that needs time: research findings, funding rounds, product launches with demos. If the news fits in one sentence, you probably don't need one.

slides.title: ask *before* you send
slides.body: Offer the news under embargo and wait for a yes. Sending embargoed material unasked and hoping it's honoured is how leaks happen.

slides.title: timezone-proof *timing*
slides.body: Write the full time and zone, and check it against the journalist's timezone.

slides.title: respect their *workload*
slides.body: Journalists are stretched: 62% took on more responsibilities this year. Give enough lead time (two to five working days for most news) and everything they need in one go.

slides.title: embargo checklist
items: News complex enough to need prep time
Date, time AND timezone in the subject line
Assets, data and spokesperson ready on day one
A plan if it breaks early

slides.title: embargo = *trust*. treat it that way.
items: Send it to whoever runs your launches

captions_meta.li_hook:
An embargo is one of the few tools that gives journalists more time to do a better story.
Used badly, it is also the fastest way to lose their trust.
li_body: Newsrooms are stretched. Muck Rack's State of Journalism 2025 found 62% of journalists took on more responsibilities this year. An embargo helps when it gives them time to prepare; it hurts when it adds admin or confusion.
li_points: Reserve it for news that needs preparation: research, funding, launches with demos.
Ask first. Share details only after the journalist agrees to the embargo.
State the date, time and timezone in full, e.g. 6:00am AEDT, Tuesday 24 November 2026.
Give reasonable lead time and send every asset in one package.
Have a plan if it breaks early: publish your own version immediately.
captions_meta.li_close: Have you had an embargo broken? What did you change afterwards?
